author: Patrick Xjr
text:
In fact sensor and finger are different : 
Blood is precise and helps to know what to do in short term ( hypoglycemia in example)
Sensor gives a trend and is there for helping to find a better way of life in order to decrease size of peek or very quick drops.
By noting what you eat you can easily identify high sugar goods and then limit quantities and frequencies…this will have an impact on HbA1c. HbA1c represents the average of sugar in your blood..and this represents another danger: sugar could block circulation in small vessels and drive to loss of eyes, loss of extremities ( foot, fingers,..+ heart attacks…)
So our illness is not so simple, we have to work on all fields together :short term actions and long term actions…
Good luck

author: Terri Smith
text: The sensors are really only good for trending info.  If I finger stick and it matches (after waiting 15 mins for fluid diff) then I’ll treat based on that for the day.  Highs and lows are always validated with a finger stick before treating.  Also sometimes I just question the value.  Again finger stick.
